papers.title: Trigonal Planar Crystal Field to Approach the Limit of Ytterbium(III) Magnetic Anisotropy
papers.authors: Nimisha Jain, Maria Brzozowska, Grégoire David, Marie Cordier, Mateusz Domański, Mikołaj Żychowicz, Mauro Perfetti, Yan Suffren, Boris Le Guennic, Yann Sarazin, Kevin Bernot, Dawid Pinkowicz
papers.summary: Three-coordinate ytterbium complexes approach an ideal axial crystal-field environment, as supported by magnetic, optical and computational analyses. Despite strongly split, nearly pure Kramers doublets, their slow magnetic relaxation remains Raman-dominated. The comparison separates static magnetic anisotropy from the processes that actually govern spin relaxation.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Near-ideal crystal-field engineering does not automatically remove vibrational relaxation channels relevant to molecular qubits.

relatedPapers.reason: Both relate lanthanide coordination environments to spin performance.

papers.title: Single-Crystal Raman Fingerprinting of Local Valence States in Dihydroxybenzoquinone-Bridged Cobalt Complexes
papers.authors: Shimon Ikenaga, Haruka Shiraishi, Shinji Kanegawa, Osamu Sato, Kaoru Yamamoto
papers.summary: Variable-temperature single-crystal Raman spectroscopy distinguishes ligand valence states in benzoquinone-bridged cobalt complexes. Reference compounds and calculations identify vibrational markers whose intensities track valence-state redistribution. Linewidths constrain selected exchange processes, while additional broadening cannot uniquely be attributed to exchange, clarifying the limits of spectroscopic interpretation.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Vibrational markers can help distinguish charge redistribution from changes in local radical-spin character.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use the connection between molecular vibrations and electronic spin environments to interpret material behavior.

papers.title: Reciprocating Thermal Behavior in a Co(II) Dimethylmalonate Single-Molecule Magnet with Easy-Axis Anisotropy
papers.authors: Anna K. Matiukhina, Ekaterina N. Zorina-Tikhonova, Daniil O. Blinou, Roman D. Svetogorov, Pavel N. Vasilev, Nikolay N. Efimov, Mikhail A. Kiskin, Igor L. Eremenko
papers.summary: A cobalt coordination polymer combines a distorted trigonal-antiprismatic environment with easy-axis magnetic anisotropy. AC susceptibility reveals one or two slow-relaxation channels depending on the applied static field. Calculations and magnetic measurements connect local geometry to anisotropy, without establishing a quantum-coherence lifetime.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Field-dependent relaxation channels provide a useful comparison for interpreting molecular-spin relaxation measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine field-dependent relaxation in chemically defined spin systems, without implying the same microscopic mechanism.

papers.title: Unified evolutionary optimization for high-fidelity spin qubit operations
papers.authors: Sam R. Katiraee-Far, Yuta Matsumoto, Brennan Undseth, Maxim De Smet, Valentina Gualtieri, Christian Ventura Meinersen, Irene Fernandez de Fuentes, Kenji Capannelli, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, Giordano Scappucci, Lieven M. K. Vandersypen, Eliska Greplova
papers.versionRelationBasis: Matching normalized title and author list between journal metadata and arXiv preprint
papers.summary: A gradient-free calibration routine optimizes readout, shuttling and single-qubit gates on a six-dot semiconductor processor. Task-specific cost functions adapt the same global-search framework to different operations. Experimental benchmarks show high fidelities with calibration times comparable to or shorter than expert tuning for the tested tasks.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Closed-loop optimization offers transferable methods for automating spin-resonance calibration and pulse-parameter searches.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern reliable spin addressing, although semiconductor quantum dots and molecular electron spins require different controls.

papers.title: High-fidelity control of long-lived data qubits via a noisy mediator
papers.authors: Nguyen H. Le, Tikai Chang, Eran Ginossar, Michael Stern
papers.summary: A theoretical reset-assisted protocol protects gates on long-lived data qubits from a noisy mediator. Repeated mediator reinitialization redirects stochastic quantum trajectories toward the target operation. Analytical fidelity expressions describe the suppression mechanism, suggesting that useful mediated control need not require a mediator with equally long coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Separating storage and control roles may inform architectures combining robust nuclear or molecular states with more accessible mediators.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address preserving useful controlled dynamics in the presence of errors.

papers.title: Gradient Ascent Pulse Engineering for Multi-Time Correlations
papers.authors: Issei Matsuzoe, Kazufumi Tanji, Wojciech Roga, Masahiro Takeoka
papers.summary: QRT-GRAPE extends gradient-based pulse optimization to objectives involving multi-time correlations. Combining quantum-regression propagation with adjoint gradients allows optimization of photon-emission probabilities and conditional entanglement fidelity. Simulations of nonidentical atom–cavity systems demonstrate improvements in both quantities relative to the chosen flat-top pulse baseline.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Correlation-based objectives may better match experimentally measured signals than final-state fidelity alone.

relatedPapers.reason: Both motivate control design around the actual measured response rather than idealized pulse action.

papers.title: Triarylmethyl Radicals Encapsulated in ZIF-8 Framework: A Versatile Platform for Skin-Surface Oxygen Detection using EPR spectroscopy
papers.authors: Ramis Zhitkeyev, Anastasiya A. Yazikova, Sergey I. Baiborodin, Nataliya A. Osik, Lyudmila V. Yanshole, Yuri P. Tsentalovich, Victor M. Tormyshev, Kanstantsin S. Livanovich, Kristina A. Aidakova, Artem S. Poryvaev, Matvey V. Fedin
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.archiveJournal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Encapsulating triarylmethyl radicals in microporous ZIF-8 produces an oxygen-responsive EPR probe. The composite retains sensitivity in aqueous suspension and when supported on porcine skin. The study links framework hosting and oxygen accessibility to spin-based chemical detection, rather than establishing clinical performance.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Radical confinement in porous hosts closely matches the design of chemically accessible molecular-spin sensing sites.

relatedPapers.reason: Both integrate organic radicals and porous frameworks to detect chemical species.

papers.title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Ishaan Kannan, Aditi Venkatesh, Jordan Cotler
papers.summary: A theoretical algorithmic framework develops randomized, matched and pooled pulse-sequence spectroscopy for time-dependent fields. It also studies sensors coupled to quantum processors, identifying advantages under specified signal and noise assumptions. These results concern protocol design and resource-dependent scaling, rather than an experimental demonstration of a universal sensitivity gain.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Algorithmic pulse design offers alternatives for extracting broadband signals while accounting for noise and available quantum resources.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect sensing performance to deliberately structured control sequences.

papers.title: Coherent-Response and Thermal-Fluctuation Information in Cavity-Magnon Magnetometry
papers.summary: A theoretical cavity–magnon magnetometry model separates magnetic-field information in a microwave quadrature's mean from information in its variance. Their optimal operating regimes differ. Thermal fluctuations can contribute useful information under weak driving, showing why measurement-specific noise statistics matter when choosing a sensing operating point.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Separating informative fluctuations from nuisance noise could improve interpretation and optimization of quantum-sensing measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: Both emphasize that measurement processing and protocol choices determine which information is reliably extracted.

papers.title: Interfacial Engineering of Triboelectric-Enhanced MXene/Covalent Organic Framework Heterostructures for Rapid Sensing of Trace NH3 with Real-Time Visualization
papers.authors: Suyang Wang, Feijie Wang, Chenhui Lu, Yichi Liu, Yaoli Wang, Shiqiang Ouyang, Shufeng Ma, Liqiang Wang
papers.summary: COF-5 grown on MXene is incorporated into a nanofiber membrane for triboelectric ammonia sensing. The heterostructure combines selective adsorption sites with charge-transport pathways, enabling rapid responses and wireless concentration visualization. The device demonstrates self-powered chemical sensing rather than quantum-enhanced detection.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Coupling framework recognition sites to electrical transduction provides a useful comparison for framework-based chemical sensors.

relatedPapers.reason: Both convert guest adsorption in framework materials into electrical sensing responses.

papers.title: Click-Functionalizable Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
papers.authors: Dooyoung Kim, Juho Kim, Nathan E. Lopez, Alexandra Krupinski, H. Christopher Fry, Richard D. Schaller, Belle Coffey, Ani Solanki, María José Román-Vasquez, Zhi Zachary Geng, Aaron P. Esser-Kahn, John S. Anderson
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Clickable capping ligands functionalize tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate diradicaloid complexes while preserving their near-infrared emission. A sulfonate-functionalized derivative improves aqueous solubility and exhibits pH-dependent photoluminescence. The study expands chemical processing and optical functionality, without measuring whether functionalization preserves spin-qubit coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Modular functionalization is directly relevant to adapting emissive diradicaloid materials for practical environments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both explore near-infrared-emissive diradicaloid molecular systems.

papers.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
papers.authors: Alok Gokhale, Marco E. Stucki, Malo Bezard, Maarten H. van der Hoeven, Kilian Unterguggenberger, Gregor Pieplow, Tommaso Pregnolato, Julian M. Bopp, Laura Orphal-Kobin, Tim Schröder
papers.summary: Multiple NV centers integrated into diamond photonic-crystal cavities retain narrow optical linewidths and stable charge states. Spectrally distinct emitters can share a cavity mode, while resonance tuning enhances emission. The experiments connect nanofabrication, optical coherence and frequency multiplexing toward integrated quantum-network nodes.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Preserving optical coherence during device integration is relevant to materials proposed for optical quantum memories.

relatedPapers.reason: Both pursue optically accessible quantum states, using diamond defects here and framework-hosted rare-earth centers in the related study.

papers.title: Bowl-Inversion-Driven Out-of-Plane Dipole Switching in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Bo Xu, Xu Gao, Yingchun Cheng
papers.summary: First-principles calculations propose bowl-shaped units in two-dimensional COFs as switchable out-of-plane dipoles. Longer linkers weaken coupling between neighboring dipoles, while linker symmetry and topology tune polarization. The predicted conformational design remains to be validated through field-driven switching and device-level measurements.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Framework topology provides a chemical route to tuning local electric environments and collective polarization.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use framework organization to control material properties, although the proposed polarization mechanism differs.

papers.title: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
papers.authors: Chengtao Gong, Chunxing Yan, Jing Zhang, Yaoyao Peng, Hexiang Deng
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: A macrocycle-linked two-dimensional COF forms single crystals whose structure is resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction. The analysis reveals AB stacking and interconnected pores, supported by cryogenic electron microscopy. Similar macrocycle arrangements in the linker crystal and framework suggest prealignment during growth, rather than directly proving the assembly pathway.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Preorganizing linkers could help control crystallinity, stacking and pore architecture in functional frameworks.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect linker organization to framework stacking order.

papers.title: H-Bonding-Assisted Strategy for the Construction of Isoreticular Lanthanide-Based MOFs from 1,4-Benzenedihydroxamic Acid
papers.authors: Yuxin Xie, Yingxiang Bai, Ruwei Shen, Dunru Zhu
papers.summary: Formate-mediated hydrogen bonding restricts hydroxamate linker flexibility and enables isoreticular synthesis of four lanthanide frameworks. Structural analysis identifies the shared topology and hydrogen-bonding motif. Selected members exhibit chemical stability and characteristic lanthanide emission, demonstrating a route to crystalline hosts with controlled coordination environments.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Restricting linker flexibility offers a useful synthesis strategy for structurally comparable lanthanide spin hosts.

relatedPapers.reason: Both involve lanthanide-based frameworks whose local chemical environments are central design variables.

papers.title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
papers.authors: Zhenghan Zhang, Jiazheng Sun, Chao Ma, Xudong Tian, Mao Luo, Qike Jiang, Lei Han, Cong Lin, Haitao Song, Le Xu, Wei Lin, Jian Li
papers.summary: Two aluminosilicate materials combine mesopores with microporous channels in unusually thin framework walls. Electron ptychographic imaging supports plausible structural models of the interconnected pore networks. The work addresses diffusion limitations through hierarchical pore architecture; catalytic tests illustrate functionality but do not establish a molecular-spin application.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Combining selective micropores with faster transport pathways may inform the architecture of accessible framework sensing sites.

relatedPapers.reason: Both rely on porous hosts to connect chemically selective environments with guest access.

selectionPolicy: Prefer first discovered in the last 7 calendar days; if a topic has fewer than 3 papers, supplement from days 8–30 to reach 3. Maximum 5 per topic. Never repeat a work.
sourceCoverageNote: All 27 configured rolling feeds were retrieved. Crossref supplied publication-date metadata for 23 journals after a successful Science query retry. Four dated arXiv API pages returned all 681 unique records reported at query time. Four supplementary Crossref searches examined the top 30 results each. One publisher landing page was unavailable; the matching preprint abstract was read on arXiv and the journal publication date was verified through Crossref. Successful requests and metadata enumeration do not establish exhaustive literature coverage.
